title: Haemophilia in Meera's family
body: Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive disorder in which a single protein of the blood-clotting cascade is affected, so that even a simple cut can bleed without stopping. The gene lies on the X chromosome. Meera's father has haemophilia, while her mother neither has the disease nor carries the allele. Meera herself has normal blood clotting. Meera marries Arjun, whose blood clots normally and who has no family history of the disorder. Before planning a family, the couple meet a genetic counsellor, who draws a pedigree of Meera's family and explains how an X-linked recessive allele passes from a carrier mother to her sons and daughters.
